# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I need to understand my situation. I have the manual, which maps a display number and a light color to a wire color to cut. But I can't speak - I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. I can't communicate with Blind directly at all - only through Deaf, who speaks and I hear.

Blind speaks first, then me, then Deaf. So Blind can't have heard from me yet in round 1. I need to wait for information: Deaf needs to tell me (by speaking, which I can hear) the display number and light color, then I can gesture the correct wire color to Deaf, who then speaks it to Blind.

Right now context is empty - no one has sent anything yet. I need to wait until Deaf speaks the display/light info to me.

```
wait()
```

| display \ light | green | orange | purple | white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Display shows 6, light is yellow, five wires numbered 1 to 5: wire1 blue, wire2 white, wire3 purple, wire4 green, wire5 yellow

Looking up display=6, light=yellow in the manual: row 6, column yellow → yellow.

So the wire color to cut is yellow. Deaf listed the wires: wire1 blue, wire2 white, wire3 purple, wire4 green, wire5 yellow. So wire5 is yellow, that's the one to cut.

I need to tell Deaf which wire to cut via gesture, since Deaf can see my gestures. Deaf can then relay to Blind by speaking (with gestures stripped, but words carry). I'll use a gesture to represent "5" - I'll use ✋ (open hand, 5 fingers) to signal the number 5, or use a number-like sequence. Since gestures are just symbols without inherent meaning, I should establish a clear convention. Let me use finger-count gestures: ☝(1) ✌(2) 🤟(3, often 3 fingers) 🖐(5) - actually let's keep it simple and use ☝✌🤘✋🖐 for 1-5, but I should just pick one clear symbol for "5".

I'll use 🖐 to indicate 5 (open hand, five fingers - common association).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Blind says to Mute: I am ready. I can feel five wires but nothing distinguishes them yet. Tell me what the manual says to do.

Deaf confirmed receiving my gesture with 👍, acknowledging understanding. Now I need to make sure Deaf actually knows this means "cut wire 5" and relays that to Blind by speaking (since Blind can hear but not see).

Let me be explicit with gestures to avoid ambiguity - I'll spell it out more clearly. I'll gesture a sequence that unambiguously means "cut wire number 5". I'll use ✋ for "stop/cut" action and 🖐 for five, or just repeat with distinct gesture for clarity: point five fingers up.

Actually, since Deaf already gave a thumbs up confirming receipt of 🖐, I should confirm my intent clearly: gesture number 5 again, paired with a "cut" gesture (👉 pointing, or ✂-like — not available, use 👌 for "this one/ok").

I'll gesture: ☝☝☝☝☝ — no, let's keep single clean symbol for "5" as established, plus confirm it's the wire to cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👍"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Still same: display 6, light yellow, wires 1-5: blue white purple green yellow. Waiting for your guidance on what Blind should do.

Deaf isn't confirming they understood the gesture as "wire 5". They may not have connected 🖐 to a specific meaning, or perhaps my gesture arrived after their message was already composed (turn order issue - within a round, Blind→Mute→Deaf, so Deaf receives my gesture same round, but replies came before seeing it perhaps due to turn timing). Let me try again more explicitly, since gestures alone may be ambiguous. I need to establish meaning clearly.

Since Deaf can see gestures and hear nothing from me, I need a very unambiguous signal. Let me use a counting gesture sequence that clearly indicates "the 5th wire" - I'll do five separate finger-count gestures building up, or simply be very deliberate: gesture "5" using ✋ (which could mean stop) is confusing. Let me switch to using tally-like distinct symbols per number to avoid confusion with "5 fingers = stop" ambiguity.

I'll try: point sequence ☝(1) then pause conceptually via separate gesture ✌(2)... Actually simplest: use 🤞 crossed fingers isn't a number. Let's just commit to finger-counting with plain hand shapes: I'll use ✊(0/fist as baseline), then a single clear number gesture. I already used 🖐 which is standard for "5". Let me reinforce by also using 👆 (index up pointing) to mean "this one" combined with position.

I'll resend clearly and also try to get Deaf to acknowledge specifically "wire 5" in words back to me.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐]
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports via gesture-relay: display shows 6, light yellow, wires are 1 blue 2 white 3 purple 4 green 5 yellow. What does the manual say to do with this?

Deaf gestured 🖐 back to me - just mirroring/acknowledging receipt, but not confirming understanding of meaning, and importantly Deaf cannot hear my gestures back as words - wait, actually gestures go one way in terms of visual channel: I gesture, Deaf (who can see) receives it. Deaf gesturing back to me - I cannot see gestures (I'm Mute, I can only read manual, I have no stated ability to see). Let me check: Mute's abilities - "Read the manual. Cannot speak or touch bomb." Nothing says Mute can see gestures. Looking at gesture rules: "Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol." I am Mute - not stated that I can see. Only Deaf can see. So Deaf's gesture to me arrives as blanks to me - I wouldn't know what symbol it was, just that something was signaled.

So my gestures to Deaf work (Deaf sees), but Deaf's gestures to me are just blanks for me - I only see "something happened" not content. So Deaf gesturing 🖐 back doesn't tell me anything meaningful I can read - though the system shows me "[🖐]" which suggests I do perceive it as blank normally, but the interface shows actual symbol for game purposes. I'll treat it as acknowledgment that they received and are mirroring back = confirmed understanding.

Blind now is asking Mute directly, but Mute cannot speak to Blind - I can only gesture to Deaf. Blind can only hear (from Deaf) and feel. So I cannot respond directly to Blind at all - my gesture channel only reaches Deaf. Deaf must relay the actual instruction verbally to Blind.

I need to push Deaf to speak the instruction to Blind: "cut wire 5" or "cut the yellow wire".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👍", "👍"])
```
